phase: Phase 15.2 resident runtime — resident lane of the frozen real100-v1 court
measured_commit_subject: phase15.4: bounded parallel CPU (rayon, non-default feature) + batch-exit semantics
tree_state: clean at court start; the 15.6 promotion edits were made after the release binary was built and are NOT in the measured binary

storage_universes_bytes.note: the resident lane adds NO storage universe; it runs against the same $d/vstore

headline_result: NEGATIVE/partial: residency alone does not pay on this corpus.

resident_vs_cold_text_repeat.all: cold v median 7 ms vs resident v_r median 9 ms -> cold 'win', resident 'loss' (both at the process/cache noise floor)
resident_vs_cold_text_repeat.mechanism: the cold `observe` path runs `narrow_probe` (a per-call manifest + derived-cache short-circuit returning the derived node without building the full Ctx), whereas `observe-batch` always evaluates the full path; its higher per-observation cost exceeds the once-per-batch process-spawn saving for documents above ~1 MiB
resident_vs_cold_text_repeat.identified_fix: hoist narrow_probe's manifest/index opens into the session so residency keeps the short-circuit (15.2 follow-up; not shipped here)

session_mixed.answered_informational: v_r is the ONLY lane that answers a heterogeneous batch; rc=0 now means the session ran and answered at least one observation (a typed per-request decline is reported on its own JSON line)

interpretation: repeated text observation costs ~1-2 ms per observation regardless of lane on this corpus; the dominant lifetime costs are ingest (encode + field-ingest) and storage, not repeated observation. Residency is therefore not the lever Phase 15 is looking for; 15.3 (packed store), 15.4 (parallel ingest) and 15.6 (adaptive promotion) are.
